title: Sales enablement kit for Benchmark Report launch (FAQ + deck + talk track)
creator: Talia Benson
description:
## Context
We’re publishing a public-facing Benchmark Report focused on production inference economics (latency and cost efficiency / “latency/$”). Sales + Solutions Engineering need a single, consistent talk track and a defensible “how we measured” story to avoid overclaiming and to handle fairness/variance objections.

This ticket produces the Sales Enablement Kit and drives alignment across PMM, Sales Enablement, Solutions, Applied ML, and Legal.

## Goals
- Provide a single source of truth for:
  - what we’re claiming (and what we are NOT claiming)
  - how we measured (high-level + where to find full methodology)
  - how to position Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private using benchmark insights
  - objection handling (fairness, variance, competitor comparisons, workload fit)
- Package assets in a way that AEs/SDRs/SEs can use immediately in:
  - outbound sequences
  - live benchmark walkthroughs
  - procurement/security conversations

## Deliverables (Enablement Kit)
1) FAQ + objection handling (doc)
- Audience: AEs, SEs, SDRs, CS
- Content: methodology summary, interpretation guidance, competitive caveats, variance expectations, replication guidance for PoCs, “what to do when prospects cite a different benchmark.”
- Location: Confluence
- Target file: sources/confluence/sales-enablement/positioning-and-messaging/benchmark-report-faq-and-objection-handling.json

2) Core message house (doc)
- Audience: anyone speaking publicly or in customer-facing settings
- Content: primary narrative, pillars, proof points, approved phrasing, disallowed phrasing.
- Location: Confluence
- Target file: sources/confluence/sales-enablement/positioning-and-messaging/benchmark-report-core-message-house.json

3) Internal launch deck (slides)
- Audience: Sales/SE/CS all-hands, onboarding new reps, manager coaching
- Content: 1-slide “what changed,” key insights, how to demo interactive page, segmentation + CTAs.
- Location: Confluence
- Target file: sources/confluence/sales-enablement/pitch-decks/benchmark-report-launch-deck-internal.json

4) One-pager (PDF/Doc)
- Audience: rep quick reference + SDR call prep
- Content: top insights, 3 bullets on methodology, approved positioning, CTA ladder.
- Location: Drive
- Target file: sources/google_drive/shared_drives/go-to-market/sales-enablement-one-pager-benchmark.json

5) SE talk track + “replicate it” PoC guidance (appendix)
- Audience: SEs doing technical walkthroughs
- Content: 10–15 minute flow, demo checklist, what to show in methodology, how to explain caching/batching, how to set up a comparable PoC.
- Location: appended to FAQ doc + linked in deck

## Key owners
- DRI / PMM: Soojin Lee
- Sales enablement stakeholders: Stephanie Nguyen (NA), Lukas Meyer (EMEA)
- Solutions/SE owner: Markus Klein
- Tech validation: Jonas Weber / Claire Dubois
- Legal approval: Michael Grant / Sofia Mendes

## Source-of-truth inputs (link here and keep updated)
- Methodology (formal): sources/confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/prompt-sets-and-benchmarks/latency-per-dollar-benchmark-methodology.json
- Validation checklist: sources/confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/prompt-sets-and-benchmarks/benchmark-data-validation-and-review-checklist.json
- Competitive notes: sources/confluence/sales-enablement/competitive/benchmark-competitive-notes-latency-cost-positioning.json
- Claims guidelines: sources/confluence/finance-and-legal/contracts-and-legal-process/benchmark-claims-legal-review-guidelines.json
- Landing page PRD/spec (for demo flow + disclaimers):
  - sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/interactive-benchmark-page-requirements.json
  - sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/benchmark-report-web-experience-spec.json

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] FAQ doc published with explicit “approved phrasing” and “avoid saying” sections
- [x] Deck includes a slide with:
  - “What latency/$ means (and doesn’t)”
  - “Variance: what’s normal vs what’s a red flag”
  - “Where to point prospects for methodology + artifacts”
- [x] One-pager distributed in Sales enablement channel + linked from deck
- [x] Legal-approved comparative language included (or removed/softened where needed)
- [x] Distribution plan executed (all-hands + pinned links + LMS upload)

## Review checklist (must pass before Sales-wide distribution)
Claims / Legal
- [x] No absolute superlatives without scoped context (e.g., avoid “fastest overall”)
- [x] Competitor references include caveats: workload, region, time window, and methodology differences
- [x] No implication that numbers are guarantees; they are measured results under disclosed conditions
- [x] Disclaimers included: variance, region capacity, model versioning, hardware differences

Technical integrity
- [x] Methodology summary matches formal methodology (prompt set, concurrency, warmup, caching policy)
- [x] Explain p50 vs p95 and why p95 matters for user experience
- [x] Explain cost metric inputs (pricing assumptions, $/token, how we compute latency/$)

Messaging alignment
- [x] Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private positioning consistent with PM/PMM narrative
- [x] CTA ladder consistent:
  - devs: “Try the API / run the quickstart”
  - scale/security: “Dedicated sizing session”
  - regulated: “Private/VPC architecture + security review”

## Notes / decisions captured
- We will standardize on the label “latency per dollar (latency/$)” in enablement, but always define it on first use.
- We will not lead with raw tokens/sec in outbound; use it as a supporting metric if asked.
- We will provide a “replication guidance” section, but clearly separate: (a) public methodology, (b) what’s hard to replicate without comparable infra.
- We will include a short paragraph on caching/batching policy to preempt the common “were you using tricks?” question.

## Launch-week usage expectations
- SDRs: use one-pager + 2 approved email snippets (linked from Ben Carter’s lifecycle variants)
- AEs: use deck slide 4–7 for quick share; direct to interactive table; offer “Dedicated sizing” CTA
- SEs: use talk track appendix; point to methodology for fairness questions; avoid debating competitor results live
